summary: DEF-001 + DEF-002 as one atomic family. Repairs the EIGHT function instances that still call the deleted public.set_rpc_context() by inlining set_config('app.rpc','1',true), matching the ten instances already repaired. Resolves the invoice-draft overload ambiguity by creating a canonical 14-argument create and a NEW canonical 9-argument update, then dropping three superseded signatures by complete signature. States ownership and privileges explicitly for all ten created/replaced signatures, revoking unreviewed PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE.

count_correction.basis: Three independent sources agree. (1) Repository: parsing every CREATE FUNCTION and CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION block in the five migrations mentioning set_rpc_context yields 15 names that ever called it. (2) LIVE: a sweep of all 368 public function bodies via mcp_list_functions found exactly 8 still calling it and 10 instances already inlining set_config. (3) The executor's unrestricted pg_proc query (2026-07-31T20:15:16Z) returned calls_helper = true on exactly those 8 rows and no others.
count_correction.no_live_only_callers: Confirmed. The DEF-020 residual risk — a function created directly on LIVE and never committed — is closed for this defect.
count_correction.audit_statements_contradicted: Invoice drafting is NOT broken (all four overloads already inline set_config), and neither is supplier payment via record_invoice_payment_safe. DEF-002's claim that one invoice-draft overload contains the DEF-001 failure is unsupported; that defect is a pure signature collision.
count_correction.incidental_drift: update_bill_draft_safe (23eac9e3) is inlined on LIVE although its git definition never referenced the helper — the December remediation touched one more function than the repository records. Recorded, not acted on.

Then exercise each live caller: bill approval, bill voiding, supplier payment, customer creation, automation rule create/edit/toggle/delete. Each must complete rather than returning 42883.

expected_objects.object: A failed update raises AND leaves existing invoice lines intact
expected_objects.verify_via: Run the OpsHealth diagnostic that creates a draft with a line named 'Original Line - DO NOT DELETE', then updates with quantity 'abc'. The call must ERROR and the original line must still be present. This is the behaviour only the strict implementation has.
expected_objects.evidence: LIVE 2026-08-03: update_invoice_draft_safe with an invalid line (quantity -1) raised 22023 'Invalid line 1: quantity must be > 0' and the invoice's existing lines were unchanged (count before = count after).

expected_objects.object: Final ACL on all ten affected signatures: owner postgres; EXECUTE to authenticated, service_role and sandbox_exec; NO EXECUTE for PUBLIC or anon
expected_objects.verify_via: Executor pg_proc: for each of the ten, proowner is postgres and proacl contains authenticated=X, service_role=X and sandbox_exec=X, and contains neither '=X/postgres' (PUBLIC) nor 'anon=X/postgres'. sandbox_exec must be present on the NEW 9-argument update_invoice_draft_safe as well as the 14-argument create - that is the amended grant. Then call one RPC with the anon key and expect a hard permission denied rather than the previous 42501 'Not authenticated' body.
expected_objects.evidence: LIVE 2026-08-03: proacl on all ten signatures is postgres=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres | sandbox_exec=X/postgres. No PUBLIC (=X) and no anon entry on any of them. Anonymous PostgREST probes return 401/42501 permission denied.

expected_objects.object: A portal user with allow_invoice_create can still create and edit their own draft invoice
expected_objects.verify_via: As a portal user holding allow_invoice_create, create a draft invoice for their own entity and edit it. Both must succeed. Then confirm the same user cannot touch another client's invoice, and cannot approve, issue, void or record payment. This is the capability the ruling required be preserved.
expected_objects.evidence: LIVE 2026-08-03: NOT verifiable and NOT passed. Any INSERT into invoices by a user holding a portal_access row aborts in the stamp_portal_provenance() trigger, which selects portal_access.contact_id — a column that does not exist (42703). This is independent of DEF-001/002 and blocks all portal invoice writes. Logged as DEF-028. Re-run this check once DEF-028 is fixed.

expected_objects.object: An organisation member WITHOUT can_create_invoices is refused on update
expected_objects.verify_via: As a member lacking the capability, call the canonical update and expect 42501. This is the one intentional behaviour change in the family and the most likely source of a 'regression' report.
expected_objects.evidence: LIVE 2026-08-03: unreachable state. can_create_invoices requires role >= 'staff', and organization_users_role_check permits only 'owner', 'admin' and 'staff' — every possible member therefore satisfies it, so 'a member without can_create_invoices' cannot exist. The adjacent guard was exercised instead: a non-member caller is refused with 42501 'Access denied to organization'. Logged as an open question (DEF-030): either the role constraint should admit 'viewer'/'manager', or the capability branch is dead code.

expected_objects.object: Create rejects a foreign entity; create and update reject a foreign customer
expected_objects.verify_via: Create with an entity belonging to another organisation -> 42501 'Entity does not belong to organization'. Create and update with a customer belonging to another organisation -> 42501 'Customer does not belong to organization'. Neither check existed in both overloads before.
expected_objects.evidence: LIVE 2026-08-03, three of three: create with a foreign entity => 42501 'Access denied to organization'; create with a foreign customer => 42501 'Customer does not belong to organization'; update with a foreign customer => 42501 'Customer does not belong to organization'.

rollback.assessment: Available but strongly discouraged. Rolling back reinstates 42883 on all eight functions (bill approval, voiding, supplier payments, customer creation, all four automation-rule operations), restores the PGRST203 ambiguity, loses the entity and customer relationship checks, and restores PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE on privileged mutating functions. Fix forward instead.
rollback.data_risk: None on apply — the migration creates and replaces functions and adjusts grants; it reads and writes no table data.
rollback.self_contained: Yes. Runs as-is inside a single transaction: all twelve pre-migration definitions embedded verbatim (eight bodies reverted to calling public.set_rpc_context(), the 14-arg create restored to 0be3f28b, the three superseded invoice-draft signatures recreated), the new 9-argument update dropped by complete signature, owner and inventoried ACLs restored. No manual insertion, no operator steps. Superseded signatures are recreated BEFORE the drop so update payloads never become unresolvable.
rollback.transaction: Exactly one top-level BEGIN; and one COMMIT;.
rollback.guard: Guarded by src/test/regression/def-001-002-rpc-context.test.ts: 12 CREATE OR REPLACE blocks, 8 restored set_rpc_context callers, DROP of the 9-argument update by complete signature, recreate-before-drop ordering, single BEGIN/COMMIT, no OPERATOR STEP text, SELF-CONTAINED AND EXECUTABLE header, file absent from supabase/migrations/. All passing.
rollback.post_rollback_verification_form: Comment-form operator queries at the end of the file (expect 8 helper callers, 4 invoice-draft overloads, ACLs carrying =X and anon). These are manual queries, not in-transaction assertions that would abort a partial rollback. Flagged, not changed.
rollback.self_verifying: Yes, and in-transaction. A DO block immediately before COMMIT asserts the end state and RAISEs on any shortfall, so a partial rollback aborts and leaves the database exactly as it was when the script started. It checks: exactly 8 functions reference set_rpc_context; exactly 4 invoice-draft overloads exist; no 9-argument update_invoice_draft_safe remains (checked by arity); and PUBLIC plus anon EXECUTE are restored on all twelve signatures — has_function_privilege raises on a missing signature, so this also proves existence. Added 2026-08-01 after the executor flagged that post-COMMIT comment queries could not self-abort.

steps: Apply 20260731210000_def_001_002_rpc_context_and_invoice_draft.sql via the Lovable migration flow. It is deliberately ONE migration: DEF-001 and DEF-002 must not exist in a half-fixed state.

post_apply_followups: The app.rpc flag is now set by eighteen functions and read by none: is_rpc_context() no longer exists and the policies that consumed it are constant false. It was inlined here only to keep the eight consistent with the ten already repaired. Deciding whether to restore the RPC-write-guard properly or strip app.rpc everywhere is a separate security-architecture task, deliberately not taken as a side effect of this repair.

The behavioural tests listed above need the Staff/Admin and second-tenant fixtures approved in Phase 0 §4 of the audit. The tests in src/test/regression/def-001-002-rpc-context.test.ts are static guards over the migration and callers; they do not execute the RPCs.

DEF-005 (mutable search_path) and the remaining 92 DEF-015 functions are both now verifiable without executor SQL, using db_rpc on mcp_list_functions with include_source — the same route that closed the DEF-001 count.

transaction_semantics.transaction_count: Forward migration: exactly one top-level BEGIN; (line 56) and one COMMIT; (line 741). Rollback: exactly one top-level BEGIN; and one COMMIT;. Verified by anchored grep and asserted in src/test/regression/def-001-002-rpc-context.test.ts.
transaction_semantics.basis: Only CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION (x10), DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS (x3), two DO blocks issuing ALTER FUNCTION OWNER / REVOKE / GRANT, and two explicit GRANTs. No CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE or ALTER SYSTEM. The eleven other BEGIN tokens are plpgsql block openers inside function bodies.
transaction_semantics.executor_wrapping: Still UNVERIFIED and unverifiable from here - the executor is not introspectable and a BEGIN/ROLLBACK rehearsal is impossible (sandbox_exec has no DDL rights). No longer load-bearing: the file wraps itself, so it is atomic whether or not the executor also wraps it.
transaction_semantics.failure_mid_file: Nothing persists; the wrapper aborts the whole file and the catalogue is unchanged. Second line of defence retained: the three DROPs sit after all ten creates, so even a hypothetical unwrapped partial state cannot leave the canonical functions missing while the superseded overloads are gone.

defects_found_during_verification.summary: approve_bill_safe writes status 'APPROVED', which bills_status_check rejects (permitted: DRAFT, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PART_PAID, PAID, OVERDUE, VOIDED). Bill approval is broken on LIVE.

create_customer_safe inserts billing_address, company_name, default_currency and internal_notes into public.customers; none of those columns exists (42703). Customer creation via the safe RPC is broken on LIVE.

stamp_portal_provenance() selects portal_access.contact_id, which does not exist. Every write by a portal user to a table carrying this trigger fails with 42703. Blocks the portal-capability verification and all portal invoice/transaction writes.

Invoice line insert casts NULLIF(v_line->>'vat_code_id','') and NULLIF(v_line->>'account_id','') straight into uuid columns with no cast, so any create/update of an invoice draft that supplies lines fails with 42804. Draft creation only succeeds with an empty lines array.

defects_found_during_verification.summary: can_create_invoices requires role >= 'staff' but organization_users_role_check permits only owner/admin/staff, so the capability branch can never refuse a member. Either the constraint or the capability model is wrong.
